This feature in WellSky is useful when searching for caregivers to fill shifts for clients. It allows you to filter for caregivers who fulfill specific criteria needed by clients for a particular shift. You can also mass message caregivers and fill shifts in real time.
These are basic activities required for taking care of oneself. These include things such as bathing, toileting, continence, dressing, feeding and mobility.

questions.field_name: What are the usual tags to include for a call log?

The scheduler called the client to inform that the aide will not be able to attend to her shift that night due to a fire incident in their apartment complex and she is still cleaning up their unit, as advised by the caregiver. The client acknowledged and stated that they do not need any aide replacement since their daughter is at home.

Mr. Parker called to ask the mobile number of his caregiver yesterday since he needs to discuss some errands for tomorrow. The scheduler acknowledged and ended the call by providing the caregiver's number to the client. This is to ensure that all information needed will be explained well to the caregiver

Your office/admin partners advised the team to remove a certain caregiver from a case due to being unreliable and deemed not fit for the case. The scheduler updated the calendar of the aide and informed her that there have been schedule changes and we'll keep her posted for updates.

Client requested to not have the caregiver she had yesterday moving forward. Client stated that the aide keeps on using her phone during her shift. The scheduler put a client block on the aide's profile and did not inform the caregiver.

Given the following image reference, create an SMS response and acknowledge the caregiver who called off.-SCENARIO: May 2nd (Friday) You received a call at 6:00 PM from caregiver Daniel informing that he won't make it to his scheduled visit with his client Harold later tonight due car problem. -Text
questions.prompt: Caregiver Daniel called at 6 PM on Fri May 2 to say he cannot make tonight's visit with client Harold due to a car problem. Write an SMS to Daniel acknowledging the call-off and asking him to keep you posted.
expected_points: addresses the caregiver by name (Daniel)
thanks or acknowledges receipt of the call-off
asks the caregiver to keep you posted or update on their condition
professional and empathetic tone

questions.field_name: Given the following image reference, create an SMS spiel to ask outgoing caregiver if they can extend.-SCENARIO: May 2nd (Friday) You received a call at 6:00 PM from caregiver Daniel informing that he won't make it to his scheduled visit later tonight due car problem.-Text
questions.prompt: Daniel called off tonight's visit with Harold due to a car problem. The outgoing caregiver is Annabel. Write an SMS to Annabel asking if she can extend her shift to cover until a replacement is found.
expected_points: addresses the outgoing caregiver (Annabel or appropriate name)
explains that the incoming aide (Daniel) called off
explicitly asks if the outgoing CG can extend their shift
mentions finding an aide replacement or that the client cannot be left alone
professional, polite, and appreciative tone

questions.field_name: Given the following image reference, create an SMS spiel to offer the open visit to our caregivers.-SCENARIO: May 2nd (Friday) You received a call at 6:00 PM from caregiver Daniel informing that he won't make it to his scheduled 8PM - 8AM visit later tonight due car problem.-Text
questions.prompt: Daniel called off his 8 PM – 8 AM visit tonight with Harold. Write a brief SMS broadcast to offer this open visit to other caregivers.
expected_points: clearly states there is an urgent open shift or coverage need
includes the shift times (8P-8A or 8PM-8AM)
asks caregivers to respond if available (by message or call)
professional and concise broadcast tone

questions.field_name: Given the following image reference, create an SMS spiel to inform the client that caregiver called off and we're still looking for a replacement.-SCENARIO: May 2nd (Friday) You received a call at 6:00 PM from caregiver Daniel informing that he won't make it to his scheduled visit later tonight due car problem. questions.prompt: Daniel called off tonight's visit with Harold. The outgoing aide has been asked to stay. Write an SMS to Harold's son Paul informing them of the call-off and that a replacement is being actively secured.
expected_points: addresses the responsible party or client by name (Paul or Harold)
informs that the caregiver called off
states a replacement is actively being sought
mentions asking the outgoing aide to stay or extend
commits to providing an update and thanks for understanding

questions.field_name: Given the following image reference, create an SMS spiel to update the client NO caregiver is available to pick up the shift-SCENARIO: May 2nd (Friday) You received a call at 6:00 PM from caregiver Daniel informing that he won't make it to his scheduled visit later tonight due car problem. Client name is Harold. Responsible Party's (Son) name is Paul.-Text
questions.prompt: After reaching out to all available caregivers, no one can cover Harold's visit tonight. Write an SMS to Paul (Harold's son) informing them that no replacement was found.

questions.field_name: OWN UNDERSTANDING | A client is exploring options to help cover the cost of ongoing homecare services. They mention having a Long-Term Care (LTC) insurance policy, while another client asks if they can use their Veterans Affairs (VA) benefits for similar services. What are the key differences between Long-Term Care insurance and Veterans Affairs (VA) benefits in terms usage for homecare services?
questions.prompt: Explain the key differences between Long-Term Care (LTC) insurance and Veterans Affairs (VA) benefits as they apply to paying for homecare services.
expected_points: notes LTC insurance is a private policy purchased by the individual
notes VA benefits are government benefits for eligible veterans
mentions eligibility differences (anyone who qualifies vs veterans/spouses)
mentions coverage/usage differences (e.g., LTC often reimburses; VA may provide direct services or aid & attendance)
explanation is coherent and demonstrates understanding, not just keyword dropping
